They've heard the term "optimization" and they like to toss it around but they haven't the first fucking clue what it actually means aside from the layman aggregate "better fps".

So you get all these people who are too stubborn to admit they don't really know what they're talking about posting reviews and, in worst case scenarios, offering scores based on their expectations as a gamer who knows how to play games and not make them. See, the problem with reviewing early access games is, I think, as much a problem with reviewing as it is with the games themselves.

We don't value games reviewers.

Print media is dying, so the old games magazines are dying too. If there's not a lot of money to pay reviewers or let them spend time playing games it affects quality, and lower circulation leads to less money and it all just spirals. Youtube reviewers who do it for a living get squeezed by dropping views on youtube and decreasing ad revenue. Online review sites have been hit with more than their fair share of issues of impartiality.

So where do you go to find out if a game is any good? At this point, my usual go-to is something like a let's play on youtube to let me see real gameplay. I also take a lot of the steam reviews of games. Not at face value, of course, but you can see if things seem like plausible criticisms that would bother you, and they're often by people who have had a longer time to play the game, and may well have fewer vested interests. If you see the same criticisms coming up again and again, then maybe those criticisms are valid.
